questions.q: Dividing $2226$ and $2529$ by a certain three-digit number leaves the same remainder $R$ in each case. Find the value of $R$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Options single digit hain, aur 'same remainder' bola hai toh seedha divisors ke difference ka game hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, jab bhi 'same remainder' aaye, dono numbers ka difference le lo. $2529 - 2226 = 303$. Ab divisor is $303$ ka hi koi factor hoga, aur question ne clearly 3-digit divisor bola hai. $303$ ke 3-digit factors hain: $101$ aur $303$. Agar main $303$ se $2226$ ko bhag dun, remainder $105$ aayega, jo options mein nahi hai. Matlab divisor pakka $101$ hai. $2226 \div 101$ par remainder $4$ aata hai. Seedha Option A tick maar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Agar $N_1$ aur $N_2$ ko $D$ se divide karne par remainder $R$ aata hai, toh unka difference $(N_1 - N_2)$ hamesha $D$ se perfectly divisible hota hai. Yahi fundamental property hum shortcut me use karte hain.

Future Exam Takeaway: CGL Mains mein jab bhi 'same remainder' dekho, HCF of differences nikalne ki aadat daalo.

questions.q: If six-digit number $5x2y6z$ is divisible by $7, 11$ and $13$, then the value of $(x-y+3z)$ is?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: $7, 11, 13$ dekhte hi dimag ki batti jalni chahiye. Ye combined divisibility $1001$ ka specific pattern hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai TestRipper, is type ka ek fix pattern hota hai. Jo number in teeno se katega, wo essentially inke LCM ($1001$) se katega.
ConceptRule
7, 11, 13 Magic MultiplierAny 3-digit number $\times 1001$ becomes $ABCABC$

Toh $5x2$ aur $y6z$ bilkul judwa (identical) hone chahiye. Compare karlo: $y=5, x=6, z=2$.
Equation mein daalo: $x - y + 3z = 6 - 5 + 3(2) = 1 + 6 = 7$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Number is form $1000 \times (5x2) + (y6z)$. $1001$ se divisibility ka matab hai alternate 3-digit blocks ka difference $0$ ya $1001$ ka multiple ho. Since it's a 6-digit number, difference exactly $0$ hi hoga.

Future Exam Takeaway: SSC me ab $1001$ ke alawa $7, 11, 13$ ka difference approach bhi puchte hain, par $ABCABC$ format sabse scoring hai.

questions.q: If $N = 1! + 2! + 3! + \dots + 50!$, then what is the remainder when $N$ is divided by $15$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: $15$ se bhag dena hai yani $3 \times 5$. Factorial series wahi end ho jati hai jahan se divisor banne lagta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, jis term me $3$ aur $5$ dono factor aa gaye, wahan se remainder $0$ aana shuru. $5! = 120$ (jo $15$ se pura katta hai). Toh $5!$ ke aage ke saare factorials ($6!, 7! \dots$) zero remainder denge.
Humein bas chillar sum karna hai: $1! + 2! + 3! + 4! = 1 + 2 + 6 + 24 = 33$.
Ab $33 \div 15$ karo, $15 \times 2 = 30$, bacha remainder $3$. Bina pen uthaye $3$ sec ka question!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Divisibility of factorials depends entirely on their constituent prime factors. Once a factorial exceeds the prime factors of the divisor, all subsequent terms are irrelevant for remainder calculation.

Future Exam Takeaway: Hamesha check karo divisor kin prime numbers se bana hai aur wo pehli baar kis factorial me combine ho rahe hain.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $(-13)^{100}$ is divided by $14$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Base $(-13)$ aur Divisor $14$ ke beech exactly $1$ ka difference hai. Seedha Fermat/Negative Remainder ka application hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, negative base dekh kar CGL me darna nahi. $(-13)$ ko $14$ se bhag dega toh positive remainder kya aayega? $+1$ (kyunki $-13 + 14 = 1$).
Ya direct deviation lagao: $(-13) \equiv 1 \pmod{14}$.
Ab us remainder par original power rakh do: $1^{100} = 1$. Itna lallu sawal free ke marks deta hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Polynomial theorem ke hisab se: $\frac{(a-1)^n}{a}$. Agar $n$ even hai toh remainder hamesha $1$ hota hai. Yahan $a=14$ aur base $14-27$ ya $-13$ le sakte hain, practically the distance to nearest multiple is what matters.

Future Exam Takeaway: Negative base hamesha modulus add karke positive remainder me convert karo, mistakes zero ho jayengi.

questions.q: How many 100-digit positive integers are completely divisible by $5$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: $5$ se divide hone ki probability hamesha $1/5$ hoti hai kisi bhi large uniform set mein.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $100$-digit numbers ki duniya me total numbers kitne hain? Pehla digit $1-9$ hi ho sakta hai (9 choices), baaki $99$ digits kuch bhi $0-9$ (yani $10^{99}$ choices). Toh total hue: $9 \times 10^{99}$.
Ab inme se $5$ se katne wale chahiye. Har $5$ lagatar numbers mein theek ek $5$ se katta hai. Toh total ko $5$ se bhag kar de: $\frac{9 \times 10^{99}}{5} = 1.8 \times 10^{99}$. Option A mark kar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Counting aur basic Arithmetic Progression (AP) ka mixture hai. Lowest 100-digit number is $10^{99}$ and highest is $10^{100}-1$. You can use $T_n = a + (n-1)d$ to find $n$, but logical probability is way faster.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi aisi massive ranges me divisibility puchi jaye, always find Total Items and divide by the Divisor directly.

questions.q: How many total digits are required to write the natural numbers from $1$ to $125$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: 1 se 99 tak fix $189$ digits hote hain. Bas $100$ se $125$ tak calculate karna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, typing wale counting sawalon me standard base yaad rakh: $1-9$ tak $9$ digits, $1-99$ tak $189$ digits. Humein $125$ tak jaana hai.
$100$ se $125$ tak kitne numbers hue? $125 - 100 + 1 = 26$ numbers. Sabme 3 digits hain.
Toh naye digits = $26 \times 3 = 78$.
Pehle ke $189$ + $78$ = $267$. Seedha calculation aur done.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Manual grouping:
1-digit ($1-9$): $9 \times 1 = 9$
2-digit ($10-99$): $90 \times 2 = 180$
3-digit ($100-125$): $26 \times 3 = 78$
Sum $= 9 + 180 + 78 = 267$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Exam me speed badhane ke lie $1-99$ ($189$ digits) aur $1-999$ ($2889$ digits) ka data direct memorize hona chahiye.

questions.q: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is $1/7$ of the number. The units digit is $4$ less than the tens digit. Find the number.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Equations mat banana shuru kar dena. 'Units digit is 4 less than tens digit' aur 'Sum is 1/7 of number' ko seedha options par test karna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, options verification sabse bada hack hai aise algebra questions me.
Option A ($84$): Tens ($8$) aur Units ($4$) ka difference $4$ hai (Condition 1 satisfied). Sum of digits = $8 + 4 = 12$. Kya $84 / 7 = 12$ hota hai? Bilkul! Dono conditions match, option A correct!
Baaki check kar lo time-pass ke lie: $62$ (sum=8, $62/7$ fraction hai - Out). $73$ ($73/7$ out). $95$ ($95/7$ out).

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Let digits be $x$ (tens) and $y$ (units). $y = x - 4$.
Number $= 10x + y = 10x + x - 4 = 11x - 4$.
Sum of digits $= x + y = 2x - 4$.
Condition: $2x - 4 = \frac{11x - 4}{7} \implies 14x - 28 = 11x - 4 \implies 3x = 24 \implies x=8$. So $y=4$. Number is $84$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Word problems regarding 2-digit numbers should ALWAYS be destroyed using Options Elimination first. Algebra is a backup.

questions.q: How many zeros are there in the product $1^{50} \times 2^{49} \times 3^{48} \times \dots \times 50^1$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Zeros depend totally on the power of $5$ kyunki $2$ ki quantity bohot zyada hai. Pattern identify karo: Base + Power ka sum hamesha $51$ hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, humein bas $5$ ke multiples ki powers extract karni hain. Multiple hain $5, 10, 15 \dots 50$. Inki powers nikal: $5^{46}, 10^{41}, 15^{36} \dots 50^1$.
Sum of powers of 5 = $46 + 41 + 36 + \dots + 1$ (ye ek AP ban gayi). Sum $= \frac{10}{2} (46 + 1) = 5 \times 47 = 235$.
Lekin $25$ aur $50$ do aese traps hain jinme $5^2$ aata hai. Yani inki powers ko ek aur baar jodna padega. $25$ ki power $26$ hai aur $50$ ki power $1$ hai. Extra zeros $= 26 + 1 = 27$.
Total zeros $= 235 + 27 = 262$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Formula for zeros is essentially extracting the prime $p=5$ using Legendre-like logical extraction over powers. You sum the primary exponents first, then secondary powers (multiples of $25$), tertiary (multiples of $125$), etc.

Future Exam Takeaway: Mixed power series me trap hamesha higher powers of 5 ($25, 125$) me chhupa hota hai, unhe alag se add karna mat bhoolna.

questions.q: Find the smallest number which when successively divided by $7$ and $8$ leaves remainders $2$ and $3$ respectively, and is a multiple of $5$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Number 'multiple of 5' hona chahiye, aur saare options multiples of 5 hain. Toh successive division se base equation bana lo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, successive division ka standard equation bottom-up chalta hai. Let last quotient be $k$.
Number $N = 7(8k + 3) + 2 = 56k + 21 + 2 = 56k + 23$.
Ab is $N$ ko $5$ ka multiple ban na hai (yani aakhiri digit $0$ ya $5$ ho).
Agar main $k=0$ lu, $N = 23$ (Fail).
Agar main $k=1$ lu, $N = 79$ (Fail).
Agar main $k=2$ lu, $N = 112 + 23 = 135$. Ye pass ho gaya kyunki last me $5$ hai. Toh smallest answer $135$ hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
To solve $56k + 23 \equiv 0 \pmod{5}$, break it down: $(55k + k) + 20 + 3 \implies k + 3 \equiv 0 \pmod{5}$. Smallest positive integer $k$ satisfying this is $k=2$. Plugin $k=2$ in $56k+23$ gives $135$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Successive division equation banakar Modulo reduction (Concept Builder method) is the most failsafe approach for CGL Mains.

questions.q: The sum of three prime numbers is $100$. If one of them exceeds another by $36$, then one of the numbers is:
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Teen prime numbers ka sum ek Even number ($100$) hai. Ye tabhi possible hai jab unn teeno me se ek Even Prime ho!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, Even prime sirf ek hi hota hai aur wo hai $2$. Toh ek number pakka $2$ ho gaya.
Ab baaki do primes ($p$ aur $q$) ka sum kitna bacha? $100 - 2 = 98$.
Question ne bola hai ek prime doosre se $36$ bada hai: $p - q = 36$.
Dono add kar do: $2p = 134 \implies p = 67$.
Aur $q = 98 - 67 = 31$.
Hamare teen primes hain $2, 31, 67$. Options mein $67$ diya hai, mark maar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Odd + Odd + Odd = Odd. But sum is Even (100). Therefore, pattern must be Even + Odd + Odd. By fixing the unique even prime (2), it converts to a basic linear system.

Future Exam Takeaway: "Sum of three primes is even" is a classic SSC Trap. Always fix $2$ as one of the primes instantly.

questions.q: Determine the last two digits of $35^{42}$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Number $5$ pe end ho raha hai, toh base ka tens digit aur power ka nature hi result decide karega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, Aman Sir ka fix rule hai:
List I (Tens Digit of Base & Power)List II (Last Two Digits)
A. Both are ODD1. $75$
B. Any other combination2. $25$

Yahan $35^{42}$ mein Tens digit $3$ (Odd) hai, aur Power $42$ (Even) hai. 'Both Odd' wali condition fail ho gayi, toh bina calculation kare seedha $25$ tick maar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Cyclicity of $5$ shows that powers of numbers ending in $5$ follow a strict modulo $100$ cycle depending solely on the parity of the preceding digit and the exponent. It's essentially $(10x+5)^{2k}$.

Future Exam Takeaway: CGL me $5$ ending values ki last two digits ke lie ye shortcut hamesha $2$ sec me answer dega.

questions.q: Find the number of factors of $6600$ which are greater than $10$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Total factors nikal kar usme se $1-10$ range wale chhote factors subtract karne hain. No direct formula, complementary counting chalegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, pehle prime factorization udhad de: $6600 = 66 \times 100 = (2 \times 3 \times 11) \times (2^2 \times 5^2) = 2^3 \times 3^1 \times 5^2 \times 11^1$.
Total factors $= (3+1)(1+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 4 \times 2 \times 3 \times 2 = 48$.
Ab $10$ tak ke numbers me check kar kon kon $6600$ ko kaat sakta hai: $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10$. (Ye total $8$ numbers hue). $7$ aur $9$ nahi kaat te.
Bache hue factors = $48 - 8 = 40$. Option A right hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Whenever asked for factors satisfying a "greater than" or "less than" bound that is relatively small, always use Total Factors $-$ Undesired Factors. It saves you from manually listing large combinations.

Future Exam Takeaway: Prime factorization me silly mistake mat karna, powers add karte waqt focus maintain rakhna!

questions.q: When $f(x) = 15x^3 - 14x^2 - 4x + 10$ is divided by $(3x + 2)$, then the remainder is:
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Polynomial Remainder Theorem seedha chillam-chilli kar rahi hai yahan. Divisor ko zero put karo, value function me daalo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $3x + 2 = 0 \implies x = -\frac{2}{3}$.
Is choti si value ko $f(x)$ mein patak do.
$f(-\frac{2}{3}) = 15(-\frac{8}{27}) - 14(\frac{4}{9}) - 4(-\frac{2}{3}) + 10$
$= -\frac{40}{9} - \frac{56}{9} + \frac{8}{3} + 10$
$= -\frac{96}{9} + \frac{24}{9} + \frac{90}{9}$ (Sabka denominator $9$ kar diya mentally)
$= \frac{-96 + 114}{9} = \frac{18}{9} = 2$.
Basic calculation thi, $2$ marks andar.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
By Remainder Theorem, dividing polynomial $P(x)$ by $(ax - b)$ yields remainder $P(b/a)$. It bypasses the tedious long polynomial division entirely.

Future Exam Takeaway: Fractions wale calculations mein LCM mentally ek step me combine karna seekho, time bachega.

questions.q: When $456753$ is divided by a certain number, the successive remainders are $44, 35, 46,$ and $51$ respectively. Find the sum of the digits of the divisor.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Ye CDS/CGL ka hardcore reverse-engineering division type hai. Long division ko visualize karke equations draw karni padengi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, step-by-step numbers likh:
Pehla operation: $456 - kD = 44 \implies kD = 412$.
Next digit laane par $447$ banega. Usme operation: $447 - mD = 35 \implies mD = 412$.
Next $355$ banega: $355 - nD = 46 \implies nD = 309$.
Last $463$ banega: $463 - pD = 51 \implies pD = 412$.
Humein divisor $D$ chahiye jo in sabko divide kare. Yani inka HCF! HCF of $(412, 309)$ is $103$.
Toh Divisor $103$ mil gaya. Sum of digits = $1 + 0 + 3 = 4$. Option A is right.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
In a standard long division process, the number formed minus the remainder gives exactly a multiple of the divisor. Taking the HCF of all such multiple-differences yields the precise divisor.

Future Exam Takeaway: Successive remainders in long division hamesha Multiples ka difference dete hain. HCF trick ko lock kar lo dimag me.

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Fractions ka LCM maanga hai. Formula clear hona chahiye: Numerator ka LCM, Denominator ka HCF.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, upar ke numbers dekh: $1, 5, 4, 8$. $4$ already $8$ ka part hai, usko hata. $8$ aur $5$ co-prime hain, toh unka LCM seedha multiply kar de $= 40$. Numerator set ho gaya.
Neeche ke numbers dekh: $6, 27, 15, 3$. In sab me sabse bada common factor (HCF) kya hai? $3$.
Dono ko mila de: $\frac{40}{3}$. Fraction ka question $5$ sec se zyada time nahi deserve karta.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
By definition, LCM of fractions must be a multiple of every numerator while being divided exactly by every denominator's maximum commonality. $\text{LCM}(a/b) = \text{LCM(numerators)} / \text{HCF(denominators)}$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Hamesha ensure karna fractions unke simplified form me hon LCM lene se pehle (yahan sab already simple the).

questions.q: Find no. of zeroes in $[100!]$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Factorial me Zeros nikalne hain, yani number of $5$s check karne hain. $100$ tak ki range me ye ek standard data hai jo yaad hona chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $100!$ ki sidhi calculation Legendre's Formula se nikalti hai. Hum successive division karte hain $5$ se.
$\frac{100}{5} = 20$.
$\frac{20}{5} = 4$.
Ab $4$, $5$ se chota ho gaya toh wahi ruk ja. Dono ko jod de: $20 + 4 = 24$. Option D answer!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
The formula is $\lfloor \frac{100}{5} \rfloor + \lfloor \frac{100}{5^2} \rfloor + \lfloor \frac{100}{5^3} \rfloor \dots$
It counts one $5$ from every multiple of 5, then a second $5$ from every multiple of $25$.

Future Exam Takeaway: $100!$ ka 24 zeroes hota hai ye directly yaad rakho, bahut baari badi values ke base calculations me use hota hai.

questions.q: If a 9-digit number $32x4115y2$, is divisible by $88$, then the value of $(4x-y)$ for the minimum possible value of $y$ is?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: $88$ divisibility hamesha $8$ aur $11$ ke combined rules se todi jaati hai. Minimum $y$ nikal ke directly $11$ ki equation me fit karo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, pehle $8$ ka rule (last 3 digits): $5y2$. Minimum $y$ pucha hai. $y=0$ rakha toh $502$ fail. $y=1$ rakha toh $512$ (jo $8$ ka cube hai) perfectly pass! Toh $y=1$ lock ho gaya.
Ab $11$ ka rule lagao (Alternating sum difference):
Odd places: $3+x+1+5+2 = 11+x$.
Even places: $2+4+1+y = 7+y$.
Difference: $(11+x) - (7+y) = 4 + x - y$.
$y=1$ yahan daal do: $4 + x - 1 = 3 + x$.
Ab isko ya toh $0$ banna hai ya $11$. Positive digits ke lie $0$ impossible hai, toh $11$ banao. $3 + x = 11 \implies x = 8$.
Humein pucha hai: $4x - y = 4(8) - 1 = 32 - 1 = 31$. Option D is right.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Isolate divisibility rules strictly. The parameter 'minimum' simplifies the search space for $y$ instantly, converting a two-variable Diophantine problem into a linear one.

Future Exam Takeaway: 'Minimum possible' aur 'Maximum possible' limits hamesha dhyan se padhna, warna correct variables aakar bhi final value galat ho sakti hai.

questions.q: Find the number of even factors of $N = 2^{5} \times 3^{4} \times 5^{3}$ which are also perfect squares.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: 'Even factor' ka matlab hai ki prime factorization me $2$ zaroor hona chahiye. 'Perfect square' ka matlab hai powers even honi chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, combinations banate hain:
$2$ ki powers: Perfect square ke lie $0, 2, 4$ chahiye. Par Even condition ne $2^0$ ko reject kar diya. Toh choice bachi: $2^2, 2^4$ (Total 2 options).
$3$ ki powers: Square ke lie $0, 2, 4$ (Total 3 options).
$5$ ki powers: Square ke lie $0, 2$ (Total 2 options).
Sabko multiply kar do (Fundamental Principle of Counting): $2 \times 3 \times 2 = 12$. Option A is correct.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
A factor $F$ is a perfect square if its prime decomposition has only even exponents. The 'even' constraint specifically forces the prime $2$'s exponent to be strictly greater than $0$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Combinatorics based factors questions me conditions ko overlapping parts me break karke independent choices multiply karna is the most robust way.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $17!$ is divided by $18$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: $18$ ek composite number hai. Wilson Theorem lagane ki glti mat karna yahan. Logical divisibility ka concept check ho raha hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, dhyan se dekh, divide kisko karna hai? $17!$ ko. Yani $1 \times 2 \times 3 \dots \times 9 \dots \times 17$.
Aur Divisor kya hai? $18$. Yani $9 \times 2$.
Teri $17!$ ki train mein $9$ aur $2$ dono aaram se baithe hain. Jab numerator mein divisor ke saare tukde already present hain, toh remainder pura $0$ bachega!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
For any factorial $N!$ and composite number $C$, if the prime factors of $C$ are fully present in the product sequence up to $N$, then $N! \equiv 0 \pmod{C}$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Factorials ke denominator me Prime aur Composite numbers ka farak clearly observe karna. Prime me Wilson chalegi, composite me basic structure.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $100^{100}$ is divided by $99$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Base $100$ aur divisor $99$ ka difference theek $1$ hai. Remainder theorem format directly dikh raha hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $100$ ko $99$ se bhag doge toh positive remainder $1$ aayega. Ab us $1$ ki power wahi laga do jo question me thi. $1^{100} = 1$.

List I (Format)List II (Remainder)
A. $\frac{(a+1)^n}{a}$1. Always 1
B. $\frac{(a-1)^n}{a}$ (n is even)2. 1
C. $\frac{(a-1)^n}{a}$ (n is odd)3. $a - 1$

Ye Format A ka sawal tha, 2 second wala.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Expand $(99 + 1)^{100}$ using Binomial Theorem. All terms except the last one ($1^{100}$) contain a factor of $99$ and are hence perfectly divisible.

Future Exam Takeaway: Difference $1$ wale formats pe free marks batorne hote hain. Table formats ko hamesha refer karo!

questions.q: How many numbers are there from $500$ to $550$ (including both) which are neither divisible by $3$ nor by $11$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: 'Neither/Nor' wale Venn Diagram set-theory type ke conditions hai. Total items me se Union minus karna hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, sequence break karo:
Total numbers $500$ to $550$ = $550 - 500 + 1 = 51$ numbers.
Divisible by 3: Sequence starts at $501$, ends at $549$. AP ke elements $= \frac{549 - 501}{3} + 1 = 17$ numbers.
Divisible by 11: Starts at $506$, ends at $550$. Elements $= \frac{550 - 506}{11} + 1 = 5$ numbers.
Divisible by Both (LCM 33): Range me pehla $33$ ka multiple $528$ hai. Range me bas yahi $1$ number aayega.
Formula laga Union ka $n(A \cup B) = 17 + 5 - 1 = 21$ (Ye divisible hain).
Humein Neither chahiye: $51 - 21 = 30$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Basic counting principle combining arithmetic progressions with Set Theory inclusion-exclusion: $N(\text{Total}) - [N(3) + N(11) - N(33)]$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab boundary 'including both' ho, toh initial count me $+1$ add karna mat bhoolna ($550-500+1$). Varna poori mehnat bekaar jayegi.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $1237^{15^{16^{17}}}$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Base ka aakhiri digit $7$ hai jiski cyclicity $4$ ki hoti hai. Nested powers dekhar ghabrana nahi, sirf power ki parity (Even/Odd mod 4) track karni hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, unit digit nikani hai toh $1237$ me sirf $7$ pe dhyan de. Ab $7$ ki power $4$ me ghoomti hai.
Power dekho: $15^{\text{Kuch Bhi}}$. Hamein bas $15 \pmod{4}$ nikalna hai.
$15$ ko $4$ se bhag doge toh remainder $-1$ (ya $3$) aata hai.
Upar power $16^{17}$ ek EVEN number hai chahe kuch bhi ho.
Toh $(-1)^{\text{Even}} = +1$. Yani actual effective power bas $1$ reh gayi.
Base $7$ pe power $1$ chadha do: $7^1 = 7$. Ye tricks Aman Sir jaisi observation mangti hain bhai!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Unit digits rely entirely on cyclicity. By finding the modulus of the exponent string w.r.t to the base's cycle length, you reduce infinite-looking exponents to a single fundamental digit.

Future Exam Takeaway: Power ke upar power ladder wale problems hamesha Modulo Negative remainders aur Even/Odd parity pe khatam ho jate hain. Base level up!

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of numbers are relatively prime?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Co-prime (relatively prime) matlab inka HCF purely $1$ hona chahiye. Options pe nazar daalo and common factors reject karo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai sidhi scanning chalegi:
Option A: $14, 21$ (Dono $7$ ke table me aate hain - Reject)
Option B: $15, 20$ (Dono $5$ se katte hain - Reject)
Option D: $18, 24$ (Dono $6$ se katte hain - Reject)
Option C: $16$ ($2^4$) aur $25$ ($5^2$). Inke prime bases alag hain, inme kuch bhi common nahi hai. Yahi tere sache co-primes hain!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Two numbers are relatively prime if their only common divisor is 1. They don't need to be prime numbers themselves, just their intersection of prime factors must be empty.

Future Exam Takeaway: CGL me definitions based aise chote sawal aate hain jahan options check karna is the fastest route.

questions.q: A natural number when successively divided by $2, 3, 5, 7,$ and $9$ leaves remainders $1, 2, 3, 4,$ and $5$ respectively. What is the remainder when the same number is directly divided by $7$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Successive division equation me beech ka modulus find karna hai toh puri chain banane ki zaroorat nahi, wahi se Modulo property laga lenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, successive division ka standard number chain banao: $N = (((((k \times 9 + 5) \times 7 + 4) \times 5 + 3) \times 3 + 2) \times 2 + 1$.
Humein iska Remainder with 7 chahiye. Let internal block $X = (9k+5)$. Humare paas hai $(7X + 4)$. Aage multiply karo aur directly Modulo 7 lo:
$((7X+4) \times 5 + 3) = 35X + 23$. Mod 7 karo: $23 \pmod{7} = 2$.
Agla block: $2 \times 3 + 2 = 8$. Mod 7 karo: $8 \pmod{7} = 1$.
Last block: $1 \times 2 + 1 = 3$. Mod 7 karo: $3 \pmod{7} = 3$.
Seedha remainder 3 aa gaya bina poori algebraic gatha likhe!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Expand the constants manually: $N = 210X + 143$. If you divide $143$ by $7$, the quotient is $20$ and remainder is $3$. The $210X$ part becomes $0$ mod $7$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Successive division ke intermediate modulo nikalne ke liye hamesha step-by-step moduli update karo, pure constants evaluate karna is a trap!

questions.q: $64329$ is divided by a certain number. While dividing, the numbers, $175, 114, 213$ appear as $3$ successive remainders. The divisor is:
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Division algorithms me consecutive intermediate remainders humein Divisor ke direct multiples dedenge via subtraction.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, Divisor guess karne ke reverse engineering ko samajh:
First step: 3 digits lo $643$. Isme se Divisor $D$ ghata ke $175$ aaya. Yani $D \times x = 643 - 175 = 468$.
Second step: Agla digit utara, number bana $1752$. Isme se ghatake $114$ bacha. $D \times y = 1752 - 114 = 1638$.
Third step: Last digit laaye, bana $1149$. Ghataya toh $213$ remainder. $D \times z = 1149 - 213 = 936$.
Ab aisa $D$ dhoondho jo $468, 1638,$ aur $936$ teeno ka factor ho (yani unka HCF).
HCF trick: $468$ aur $936$ clearly $468$ me related hain ($468 \times 2 = 936$). Ab $468$ aur $1638$ ko dekho, $468$ ka half $234$ kya dono me lag raha hai? $234 \times 7 = 1638$ aur $234 \times 4 = 936$. Yes! Toh Divisor = $234$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Long division steps strictly equate to: $\text{Dividend block} - \text{Divisor Multiple} = \text{Remainder}$. Collecting all difference equations provides numbers that all share the Divisor as a common factor.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi intermediate remainders diye hon, unhe 'New Formed Dividend' se subtract karke seedha unka HCF nikal lo.
